discovery: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene and the creation of moiré flat-band quantum materials

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics / nanoscale and two-dimensional materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted in 2011 that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees would flatten the electronic bands, so that interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group fabricated such devices and found correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity. Many laboratories have since reproduced these results, and they are robust. The work turned the twist angle between atomic layers into a new control parameter for quantum matter. It started the field of moiré materials, which has since produced orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, and fractional Chern insulators at zero magnetic field. Nanoscale fabrication here did more than refine an old system: it created a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics, built by stacking. Few recent discoveries have changed so profoundly what experimentalists believe can be made and measured.
